Package ca.refundr.highspring.api.jetty

Class RequestFilter

java.lang.Object
ca.refundr.highspring.api.jetty.RequestFilter
All Implemented Interfaces:
jakarta.servlet.Filter
public final class RequestFilter extends Object implements jakarta.servlet.Filter
Servlet filter that is the front door for every API request.

What happens on each call (read this first)

  1. Apply CORS headers so the Remix app on another origin can call us.
  2. Open a RequestScope (DB access, JSON helpers, etc. for this one request).
  3. Turn the URI into a path like v1/products/ (no leading slash).
  4. Build a RootResource and call getByPath(path) to find the handler (see
    invalid @link 
    {@link ca.refundr.highspring.api.resource.package-info
    }).
  5. Run matching.processRequest() → httpGet/httpPost/…
  6. Write the ServerResponse to the servlet output.

Exception policy (important for production)

  • RequestFailedException — expected 4xx (auth, forbidden). Answer only; do not log to DB.
  • PurchasesResource.ProductNotFound — 404 for unknown catalog ids.
  • BadRequestException — 400 for bad client input / empty cart / bad JSON.
  • Any other Exception — 500, full stack saved to api_error_log, email developer.

Jetty is configured so this filter runs for all dispatcher types; otherwise requests can mysteriously 404 before reaching our code.
